why_relevant: Complete enumeration of the 11 licensed ME banks with per-bank profile pages; the canonical actor list to which every LinkedIn company page must be mapped, and it flags smaller banks (Ziraat, Zapad) easily missed.

source_name: CBCG register of banks — 'Banks in Montenegro' useful-links page
why_relevant: Authoritative actor list (licensed banks and, elsewhere on the site, payment institutions) that anchors the LinkedIn cell: every registered entity should have its LinkedIn presence checked, and absence of a page is itself a finding.

source_name: Tracxn — payments startups in Montenegro (people/founder profiles)
why_relevant: Enumerates c.17 ME payments startups (PencePay, XCHPay.me, LocalPay, Sharej, 4On) — the non-bank PSP actor list whose LinkedIn pages and founder profiles then become trackable hiring/leadership sources.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC) — member list and board/leadership pages
why_relevant: Bank CEOs sit on the MFIC board; changes there (e.g. an MFIC president stepping down to take a new banking role) are a reliable indirect leadership-move signal, and MFIC posts these on LinkedIn.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro — employee LinkedIn profiles (no confirmed company page)
why_relevant: For the smallest licensed banks (Ziraat, Zapad) no LinkedIn company page surfaced; individual employee profiles are then the only professional-network visibility into their staffing and org units.

source_name: Bankar.me — Banke u Crnoj Gori (bank directory / actor map page)
why_relevant: A maintained list of the banks operating in Montenegro. Serves as the actor map that drives every other query in this cell: it enumerates the official Montenegrin-language legal names and aliases (CKB, NLB, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, Zapad, Adriatic, Prva, Universal Capital, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) that leadership-move searches must be run against.

Montenegro's largest independent daily/portal and the outlet most likely to report contested personnel events banks will not announce: dismissals, resignations under pressure, union disputes, branch closures, supervisory-board conflicts. Investigative desk means it also names people whose appointments are politically contested.

Montenegro's oldest daily, historically state-linked, with a business desk that routinely carries appointment notices, AGM/board-formation reports and interviews with bankers. Its editorial line differs from Vijesti, so it often carries the institutional/appointee side of a contested personnel story that Vijesti frames critically — valuable for triangulation.

High-volume general news portal with a daily economy stream; fast on press-release-driven appointment news and on branch-closure/reorganisation items. Good breadth-and-speed complement to the slower dailies.

source_name: RTCG — Radio Televizija Crne Gore, Ekonomija
why_relevant: Public broadcaster. Slower and more institutional than the portals, but it is the outlet that carries on-camera interviews with newly appointed CBCG governors and bank CEOs, and it reports parliamentary/board appointment procedures in detail. Its output is also the least likely to be paywalled or later deleted.

source_subtype: general news portal with business vertical
why_relevant: Montenegro's first news portal (founded 2009, Podgorica) with a dedicated business vertical 'Abiznis' carrying finance and corporate-management coverage. Note: the intuitive domain analitika.me is NOT this outlet — the correct domain is portalanalitika.me. A named cell target, so getting the domain right matters.

source_name: Ekonomist.me — Montenegrin business & fintech online magazine
why_relevant: Podgorica-based business/finance magazine (founded 2014, publisher BePositive, founder Ljiljana Premović), described as Montenegro's only fintech-focused portal. Directly on-sector for payments as well as banking, and the kind of outlet that runs profile interviews with newly appointed executives and fintech hiring stories that general dailies ignore.

Independent radio station plus news portal (portal founded 2016 by Darko Šuković) with a standing economy section. Editorially combative and interview-heavy, so it is a likely venue for a dismissed or resigning banker to give their side — the kind of first-person account no official channel produces.

High-traffic Montenegrin news portal. Politically aligned and lower-credibility than the dailies, but it publishes patronage-and-appointment stories about state-linked institutions early and aggressively; useful as an early-warning tripwire that must always be corroborated before use.

Montenegrin news portal with an economy stream; adds redundancy so that a personnel story is not missed if a primary outlet is blocked or deletes an item. Also carries regional (Serbian/Bosnian) bank-group news relevant to parent-company reorganisations that cascade into Montenegrin subsidiaries.

Montenegrin news portal with a standing economy rubric. Secondary breadth source for appointment notices and corporate reorganisation items; useful for catching stories that only get PR-wire distribution.

Politically aligned Montenegrin portal. Low credibility for facts, but it reports dismissal and patronage allegations about state-linked financial institutions that mainstream outlets sit on. Value is as a tripwire only — every claim needs corroboration before it enters the intelligence record.

Local/city-level Montenegrin portal. Branch closures and small-town bank staff reductions are frequently reported only at local level — a national desk will not cover the closing of a single filijala in Bijelo Polje or Berane, but a local portal will, and that is a real organization-change signal.

Podgorica city portal. Same rationale as Gradska.me but for the capital, where most bank head offices and the largest branch networks sit; picks up head-office relocations, office openings/closures and local hiring drives.

source_name: Media Ownership Monitor Montenegro (Reporters Without Borders / partner)
why_relevant: A structured inventory of Montenegrin media outlets with ownership, reach and audience data. This is the authoritative pointer for completing and bias-weighting this cell's source list: it tells you which portals exist, who owns them, and therefore whose reporting on a contested bank dismissal is likely to be politically motivated. Directly supplies the credibility priors used above.

source_name: Bank official social accounts amplifying local media interviews (e.g. Erste Bank Montenegro Facebook)
why_relevant: Montenegrin banks reshare local-media interviews with their own executives, which surfaces the interview (and the executive's current title) even when the originating outlet is bot-defended or has removed the article. Observed: Erste Montenegro promoting a Bankar.me interview with its CEO Aleksa Lukić. Acts as a resilient mirror layer and a title-verification cross-check for this cell.

source_name: eFirma / CRPS portal (Uprava prihoda i carina) — registration and filing front end
why_relevant: The modern e-portal through which registrations and changes (including change of legal representative) are filed and published; the operational successor front end to the older crps.me pages, run by the Revenue and Customs Administration.

source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Beneficial Ownership Register), CRPS/eFirma
why_relevant: AML-mandated register of ultimate beneficial owners of Montenegrin entities, held inside the CRPS system since Aug 2021. Reveals control changes behind banks, payment institutions and fintech vehicles that a pure director listing misses.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette) — online document search
why_relevant: Publishes rješenja/odluke on appointments and dismissals (imenovanje, razrješenje) for state-linked financial bodies — Central Bank council members, state-owned/state-participated banks, regulators — plus the statutes and by-laws that reshape bank governance (e.g. the two-tier management/supervisory board regime).
Commercial consolidation of Montenegrin legislation with an 'updated regulations' feed — a faster, better-indexed way to spot new banking/payments by-laws and governance rules than the raw gazette.
Authoritative current listing of Governor, Vice-governors and Council — the regulator's own leadership changes, which parliament/gazette formalise.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala — Centralni registar propisanih informacija (CRPI)
why_relevant: Statutory central repository of regulated disclosures by listed issuers — several Montenegrin banks are issuers, and board/management changes are disclosable events filed here with dates, making it a near-real-time leadership-change feed.
